name: Inca (Quechua)
description: Quechua dark constellations: animal shapes seen in the dark lanes of the Milky Way rather than among bright stars. Polygons are schematic approximations.
source: Urton, G. (1981) At the Crossroads of the Earth and the Sky: An Andean Cosmology, University of Texas Press (Quechua dark-cloud constellations, Misminay, Cuzco region)
license: Original compilation (CC0 for the coordinates); factual references only, no text copied from the sources

figures.name: Yacana
figures.story: Dark-cloud llama of the Milky Way lane, with its head toward the Coalsack. Described in Quechua tradition by Urton (1981) and earlier chroniclers. The outline is a schematic, approximate region of the Milky Way dark lane, not a measured boundary; consult the source for the figure itself.

figures.name: Yutu
figures.story: Dark-cloud tinamou (partridge-like bird) near the Southern Cross, per Urton (1981). The outline is a schematic, approximate region of the Milky Way dark lane, not a measured boundary; consult the source for the figure itself.
